notes: TWO RELEASES IN ONE UPDATE: THE RECONCILIATION SCREEN OPENS AGAIN, AND IT SAYS MORE ABOUT WHAT IT KNOWS. THE SCREEN OPENS STRAIGHT AWAY. Opening Bank Reconciliation stalled for around half a minute, on every machine, with the spinning wait cursor. It was the queries, not the computer: work that only needed doing once was being redone for every entry on the account, several times over. On a real ledger of 358 cheques and 1,451 entries, about thirty seconds of waiting is now under one. NO FIGURE CHANGES: the same reconciling items, the same totals, checked against seven filed months before release, every one of which still reproduces to the penny. THE EXCEPTIONS PANEL STOPS CRYING WOLF. The yellow panel naming cheques the register and the ledger disagree about was flagging one where nothing is wrong. An opening cheque is brought forward with no issuing voucher; when it goes stale the write-back becomes the only voucher on the record, and that write-back DEBITS the bank, because the cheque dies while the debt survives as a creditor. Comparing the cheque's face value against its own write-back reported it out by twice its value, permanently. It is no longer listed. A reinstated ordinary cheque is still checked, because its payment and its write-back are two different vouchers and there is a real figure to compare. WHAT THE STATEMENT HORIZON IS KEEPING OUT. The schedules built from imported statements can only reach back as far as your earliest imported statement, and the note underneath says how much lies behind that date. It was counting EVERY ledger entry on the account, when only a fraction could ever have appeared as a reconciling item. On a real account the headline was 355 entries where the answer was 18: the rest carry cheques, so they belong to the cheque schedule, not to money that left the bank with no cheque. Your opening balance is not in the figure either. It is the bank's position on day one, not a payment waiting for a cheque, and since the note's own advice is to import an earlier statement, a figure that included it would have been advice worth ignoring. A MONTH SIGNED OVER A KNOWN DISAGREEMENT NOW SAYS SO. You could sign a month with the exceptions panel showing rows, and the filed version kept no record that anything had been standing. Signing now asks, naming the cheques, and the filed version records what the panel said at that moment. A month signed clean records an empty list, which is an answer rather than a silence. It still does not refuse: a registered amount can differ for a timing reason that resolves itself, and stranding a close over it would turn the panel into something to work around rather than read. The signed versions list gains an Exceptions column. A STATEMENT THAT RUNS PAST THE MONTH END. Bank files routinely carry the first days of the next month. Reconciling August, the statement window listed September's transactions and offered them for matching, and matching one clears the item on the BANK's date, in a month you have not started. Lines after the statement date are now set aside and counted on screen, with one press to bring them back if you mean to work ahead. The items offered for matching are those outstanding as at the date being reconciled, rather than as at today. PAYROLL APPROVAL CANNOT BE WRITTEN ROUND. The approval step refuses to let whoever ran a month approve it, but nothing stopped the status being set directly and the month then posted. Approval now happens only through Approve, and the facts the rule depends on are frozen: who ran the month, who approved it, when, and which month a payslip belongs to. A FILED SIGN-OFF IS SIGNED BY WHOEVER SIGNED IT. The reconciliation history keeps every signed version and cannot be edited or deleted, but the name on the record came from the app rather than the database. On a record that cannot be edited, a wrong name is permanent. The signer and the time now come from the server, and the version number is allocated in the same step that writes the row, so two people signing the same month at once cannot collide. SMALLER THINGS. The overdue badge on staff advances reads the ageing from the ledger rather than working it out again on the screen, so there is one definition of late, and it says so plainly if that reading fails instead of showing no badges and looking like nothing is overdue. INSTALLING: no data changes and no ledger entries in this update. It installs straight over the previous version, but please still take a backup first: Backup and Export, Back up now.
